title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Promotion: 20% off
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted lift from 18 past promotions: x2.09; this week's price drop is 16.4%, slightly less than 20% off, but still strong. Baseline already reflects trend, so full x2.09 is appropriate.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: No prior data on this event, but plausible demand loss. Use moderate downside adjustment due to uncertainty. Pooled department data shows 10-20% loss from similar events.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween shows no consistent lift (noise-adjusted x1.0), so no effect. The 20% off promotion has strong historical lift (noise-adjusted x2.09), but the price drop is deeper (16.4% vs 20% off) and the baseline already reflects recent trends. The competitor opening adds downside risk: not seen before, but plausible demand cannibalization. Shrink uplift toward 1.0 due to thin evidence on competitor impact and deeper discount. Combine multiplicatively, then shrink to account for uncertainty.

PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (3 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat); Promotion: 20% off
  shelf price: 8.26 (-16.4% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.8 - 233.5 | 10%-90%: 67.3 - 191.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
